title: Menger's theorem: arc version for digraphs
statement: Let $D$ be a finite digraph, and let $x$ and $y$ be two of its vertices. Then the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths from $x$ to $y$ equals the minimum number of arcs whose deletion destroys every directed path from $x$ to $y$.
hypotheses_covered: x and y are vertices of D
replaced:
(Menger, 1927; arc version for digraphs). \emph{Let \texttt{x} and \texttt{y} be two
vertices of a digraph \texttt{D}. Then the maximum number of arc-disjoint directed
\texttt{(x, y)}-paths in \texttt{D} is equal to the minimum number of arcs whose
deletion destroys all directed \texttt{(x, y)}-paths in \texttt{D}.}
